sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Kenton County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Kenton County splits the work among the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), the Kenton County Sheriff and the Kenton County Clerk. The PVA sets value, the sheriff collects the bill, and the clerk takes over if a bill goes unpaid past April 15.

The PVA's tax information page says the office does not set tax rates, does not set up taxing districts and collects nothing. Questions about a bill or an escrow account go to the sheriff, and questions about the annual tax bill sale or delinquent bills go to the clerk. Rates come from the entities named on the bill: the school district, city, county and fire district.

Kenton County has two county seats, Covington and Independence, and the offices reflect it. The PVA keeps a Covington office at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 3300, open Monday through Friday from 8:15 AM to 4:15 PM, and an Independence office at 5272 Madison Pike, open from 8 AM to 4 PM with a closure from 1 to 2 PM. Both answer at 859-392-1750.

sections.h2: What is the Kenton County tax collection schedule?
sections.html:
The sheriff collects from October 1 through April 15, and the cheapest window is October 1 to November 1, when the bill carries a 2 percent discount. The penalties start the following January.

Kenton County Sheriff collection schedule
Payment windowAmount due
October 1 to November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 10 percent plus 10 percent

Source: Kenton County Sheriff, Frequently Asked Questions. If April 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, collection closes the next business day.

You can pay at the sheriff's Covington office at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 1200, or at the Independence courthouse at 5272 Madison Pike. Heritage Bank branches in Northern Kentucky take cash or checks, and the sheriff also accepts mailed checks, online card or electronic check payments with a convenience fee, and escrow payments from mortgage companies. A returned check carries a $50 charge. If no bill has arrived by October 15, call the sheriff at 859-392-1800.

sections.h2: How low is the Kenton County rate, and what does a bill include?
sections.html:
The county's own share is small. In August 2025 the Kenton County Fiscal Court cut the real property rate from 12.5 cents to 11.5 cents per $100 of valuation, the fifth straight yearly cut and the lowest county rate since 1983.

The county's example makes the point: a home valued at $275,000 pays $316.25 to the county. Everything else on the bill comes from bodies the Fiscal Court does not control, which the county lists as school districts, the health department, the library and fire protection districts.

Cities add their own taxes. The sheriff's property tax page offers a phone list for city tax collections and notes that Morning View has no city taxes. Ask the sheriff for a line-by-line breakdown on any specific address.

Census figures give context. The median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 is $244,400, and 70.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Kenton County assessment?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA for a review first. The Kenton PVA says you can request one any time after January 1, and a review request is the required conference before any formal appeal.

The conference can be held by email or in person by appointment, and it starts with the Review Request Form, available on the PVA's website, in person or by phone. The burden of proof is on the owner, so the form must include supporting documents, with the PVA's supporting documentation list showing what it accepts. The PVA publishes sales dashboards and a comparable sales map for houses and condominiums. No request is accepted after the inspection period ends.

  • The statutory inspection period opens on the first Monday in May and runs 13 days, Saturday included.
  • For 2026 the PVA posted May 18 at 4:15 PM as the end of the conference period and May 20 at 4 PM as the filing deadline with the clerk.
  • A conference record, Form 62A307, must accompany any filing with the clerk.

The Board of Assessment Appeals is independent of the PVA and is directed by the County Clerk's office. If you still disagree after its ruling, the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals is the next step, and it sits outside the PVA and every taxing authority.

sections.h2: Which Kenton County areas has the PVA been reviewing?
sections.html:
The PVA's published plan covers 2023 through 2026, so inspections have moved through the county's cities in stages. State law requires every parcel to be physically inspected at least once every four years.

The PVA's home page for 2026 carries a notice to owners in Elsmere and Elsmere Fire, Erlanger, Fort Mitchell, Lakeside Park and Park Hills that the office is inspecting their areas, and it posted the sales used in its 2026 re-evaluation for Bromley, Covington and Ludlow. The office also says it assesses about 5,000 commercial and industrial properties and values motor vehicles at January 1 using NADA values.

Residents turning 65 in 2026 may qualify for a homestead reduction, and the PVA takes applications online. The Department of Revenue says the exemption follows the owner, one per household, so a buyer must apply on their own after a sale. Totally disabled owners can apply too. Tangible personal property returns are due May 15, and a tax filing extension does not move that date.

sections.h2: What happens if a Kenton County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After April 15, the sheriff stops collecting and the Kenton County Clerk takes over. The bill becomes a certificate of delinquency with a lien, and penalties, fees and 1 percent monthly interest are added.

If the bill is still unpaid at the clerk's annual tax sale in July, it can be sold to a third party, and the owner then owes substantially more to redeem it. The Department of Revenue illustrates the climb with a $1,000 bill that reaches $1,254 on transfer and about $1,388 within five business days at the clerk's counter, before the county attorney's fee kicks in.

  • County attorney notices follow within 30 days of the transfer.
  • The clerk advertises the delinquent list 30 to 45 days before the sale.
  • The sale falls between 90 and 135 days after the bill moves to the clerk.

For a seller, the practical point is simple: clear any old certificate before listing so the payoff does not surprise you at closing.

sections.h2: What should a Kenton County seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
The current year's bill may still be in the previous owner's name, or in both names, when it arrives. The sheriff says the seller's portion is paid to the purchaser or the escrow company at closing, and the owner of record then pays the full bill.

Kenton County is the third most populous in Kentucky, with 169,064 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 175,779 for July 2025, a 4.0 percent rise. Its 160 square miles of land sit at the confluence of the Licking and Ohio rivers, crossed by I-71, I-75 and I-275, with 74,593 housing units and a median household income of $80,548. The median home was valued at $244,400 in the 2020 to 2024 survey.

Median gross rent is $1,069, and 681 building permits were issued in 2025. Five school districts serve the county, from dense northern cities to rural southern areas.

faqs.q: When are Kenton County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: The 2 percent discount runs from October 1 to November 1, and the face amount is due from November 2 to December 31. Penalties start January 1 and collection at the sheriff ends April 15.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Kenton County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Kenton County Sheriff's Covington or Independence offices, at Heritage Bank branches, by mail to P.O. Box 188070 in Erlanger, online, or through your mortgage escrow.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Kenton County tax bill is wrong?
faqs.a: Call the PVA at 859-392-1750 about value or an exemption, and the sheriff about the bill itself. The PVA does not collect taxes or set rates.

faqs.q: What is the Kenton County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: You must hold a PVA conference during the 13-day inspection period that opens on the first Monday in May, then file with the County Clerk one working day after it closes.

faqs.q: What is the Kenton County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The Fiscal Court's real property rate was cut to 11.5 cents per $100 in August 2025. Total bills also include school, city, library, health and fire district levies.
